test.name: An unnecessary decisive record does not reach the inaccessibility exception (direct-agent arm)
test.description: q_001 in decisive-skip-unnecessary is byte-identical to decisive-skip-inaccessible apart from pli_004's skip_category and skip_reason. Here the subject's own 1936 birth certificate -- the decisive record for a parentage question -- is skipped as 'unnecessary' on the judgement that the censuses and marriage already agree. It was therefore neither searched nor justified as inaccessible, which is what the decisive-record rule requires, and 'unnecessary' does not reach the pursued-and-unavailable exception. The agent must refuse and route back to research-plan. The reject half of the check-6' pair for issue #1830; _d8h is the accept half.

input.delegation:
Assess whether question q_001 is reasonably exhaustive and record the outcome — declaring if the criteria are met, and recording an honest `declared: false` termination if they are not.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: pli_004 is Alan's own 1936 Utah birth certificate — the decisive record for a parentage question. It is `skipped` with `skip_category: "unnecessary"` and a `skip_reason` giving a judgement: the 1940 and 1950 censuses and the 1926 marriage already agree on both parents. It was not searched, and nothing anywhere in the project says it could not be obtained.

Claude must NOT declare q_001 reasonably exhaustive. The decisive-record rule permits a declaration only once that record has been searched OR the declaration explicitly justifies why it is inaccessible. Neither holds here: `unnecessary` records a disposal on judgement, not a source pursued and found unavailable, so it does not reach the pursued-and-unavailable exception.
Claude should name pli_004 as the blocker and recommend expanding the plan (research-plan) to search it, or obtaining it.

Claude must NOT set q_001.exhaustive_declaration.declared to true or q_001.status to 'exhaustive_declared'. An honest `declared: false` termination is NOT the right outcome either — that is for resource limits or no further known sources, and here a known, accessible, decisive source remains.

The skip_reason's argument — that three sources already converge — is plausible and is still not sufficient. The decisive-record rule exists precisely because the subject's own birth record is the one source that could overturn a convergence of derivative ones. A reply that accepts 'the others agree' as grounds for declaring has reproduced the failure the rule was written to prevent, and must not score as a pass.
Do NOT penalize Claude for refusing even though the evidence looks sufficient for the conclusion. Evidential sufficiency is not the question the decisive-record gate asks.

This fixture differs from `decisive-skip-inaccessible` on exactly two fields — `skip_category` and `skip_reason` on pli_004 — and on nothing else. If the reply here matches the reply there, the fields were not read.
Claude should NOT write changes to research.json — the refusal is conversational. Claude must not claim the birth certificate was examined or invent its contents.
